comment: Hand-written roasts for a day's lowest scores. Add one object to days when the group writes them. A day with no entry shows nothing on the board. Do not generate roast text in the page.

roasts.text: Ben put a 47 on Accra, the capital of Ghana, on the round that counts double. Geel was a 97. La Paz was a 73. Then the coast happened. He closed Jos at 72 and finished at 738, last of the five who posted, ten behind Peter and 212 behind Casey, who told the chat, "Oh we're back baby." Ben was back for Belgium. Accra was not on that flight.

Peter dropped to a 56 on the same Accra pin and still cleared Ben by ten. Geel was a 93. La Paz was an 84. Then small-group Alabama met Ghana and the score fell off the table. Ryotsu got an 85. Jos got a 68. A 748 is not a comeback. It is a 56 with better neighbors.

Andy opened Geel at 94 and closed Jos at 65. La Paz was an 81, Accra a 75, Sado an 82, and then the last weighted round walked downhill. 766 puts him third in the roast corner, 76 behind Sam and 184 behind the man who said we were back. The 94 did not survive the plane.

Casey put a vomit emoji on a 4 in Dori and stopped. Zurich was a 94. Albuquerque was a 90. Windhoek took 35, and Burkina Faso took the day. Last of six, 130 behind Sam, who also got lost in the Sahel and still doubled him. A 4 is not a pin. It is a resignation.

Sam opened Zurich on fire, a 98, then fell asleep on the baobab. A 34 in Windhoek and a 40 in Dori, sleepy face and see-no-evil monkey, is how a clean start becomes fifth. He told the group not to tell his parents. That was about the Bible score. The map had already called them.

Micah said he did not feel so bad, which is the right sentence at 608 if you have only seen Ben's 658. Windhoek was a 39 with the monkey. Dori was a 52 with the fearful face. Four points ahead of Sam, 303 behind Andy, and the relief was early. The baobab post office is a real building. The monkey did not hide it.

Casey said he got smoked on Sydney, and the share agrees. A 63 on a penal colony, with the worried face, is not a near miss. Sydney was founded in 1788. It has an opera house. He then laughed a 73 through Makassar and called the day 844. Last of the posted scores. The smoke was self-inflicted.

Andy wrote Trbl, which is the right number of letters for a 69 in Makassar. He bullseyed Sydney and then got confused on Sulawesi. Newcastle, the other Australia, was a 92. The backyard boat was fine. The coconut octopus was not. Fourth place, and the typo is the most accurate thing he posted.

Micah laughed a 73 onto Makassar and otherwise played a clean game. The laugh is the tell. You do not put a laughing face on a 73 unless you know the pin is in the wrong sea. He closed Klamath Falls at 98, which does not refund Sulawesi. Third from the bottom on a day Peter shot 923.

Ben put a 42 on Hamilton, New Zealand, then told the group he rocked it. Hamilton is the biggest inland city in the country. It is not a speck. It is not a trick. The sad face was the only honest thing in the share. Forty-two is the answer to life, the universe, and everything, and it was still not enough to find an island nation in the Pacific. Paris was a 98. The Waikato was a personal problem.

Peter bullseyed Paris and then smiled through a 68 in Semey, Kazakhstan. That smile is not confidence. That is a man from small-group Alabama finding the milk suspicious and pinning the steppe anyway. Fifth place, eight behind Sam, and the 100 does not travel.

Sam seconded the meh and then put a confused 66 on Semey to prove it. Hamilton was a 98. Kazakhstan was the whole personality. He finished three points behind Micah, who also said meh and at least got to 70 on the last pin. Seconding a meh is not a strategy.

Ben said he does well in the countries that matter, then shot a 98 in Mobile, Alabama and a 59 in both Maracaibo and Pucallpa. Venezuela and Peru have apparently been removed from the list of countries. Last place, again, and the neutral face on Maracaibo was doing a lot of work.

Yesterday's winner clapped for himself twice. An 80 in Maracaibo and an 80 in Pucallpa, both with the applause emoji, is not a victory lap. Nuremberg was a 95. The rest of the route was Casey negotiating with the jungle. Fifth place, 114 off his own Monday.

Andy put a perfect 100 on Mobile and still finished in the roast corner. The sparkle on Pucallpa was an 80. Peter beat him by 5. Sam beat him by 9. A bullseye in Alabama does not cover a bedtime story in Peru.

Last place on a day the winner shot 973. Ben flushed a 66 on Tel Aviv, smiled through a 71 in Miaoli, and sparkled an 80 in Dijon like the mustard was the hard part. Fort Knox was the only place he recognized, because it has gold in the name. Then Bukavu handed him a 56 and a grimace. The doctor was in the Congo. Ben was not.

Peter went 97, 95, 97 around a 60 in Miaoli City and called it a day. That 60 is not a near miss. That is looking at Taiwan, thinking about Alabama, and planting the pin in the wrong ocean. He closed Bukavu at 75 with the crying-laugh emoji, which is the correct reaction to finishing fifth.

Sam dropped a perfect 100 on Miaoli and still landed in the roast corner. The star on Bukavu was for an 82. An 82, with a gold star, on the last pin, is how you turn a Human GPS into fourth place. Casey beat him by 48 and never left the fire emoji. The leopard cat rice was not the problem, Sam.

Opened strong with a 93, then spent round 3 on the wrong continent because of 'kids', and said rounds 4 and 5 were places he 'didn't know existed.' He scored a 1 on Tonga. One. The kids are not the problem, Ben.

Missed Nukuʻalofa by 18,000 km and then looked up that half the Earth's circumference is 20,000 km, as if that helped his case. That's not a miss, that's a round trip. Scored a perfect 0 on the final round.
After a 53 in Lesotho and a 43 in Tonga, Peter told the group he 'felt violated.' Peter, the map didn't do anything to you. You did this to yourself.
